subject: MapleBridge + Redwood: runtime curation & SDK integration
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@maplebridge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, MapleBridge Partnerships <partnerships@maplebridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MapleBridge + Redwood: runtime-curation integration proposal

Hi Vanessa,

Appreciate the intro — I'm Daniel (Head of Partnerships at MapleBridge). We build a developer SDK used by ~120 teams for composing multi-step LLM workflows (LangChain & LlamaIndex flavors, tracing hooks, prompt toolkits). We've had a number of customers ask for a "Redwood Verified" runtime bundle so they can run our SDKs against your hosted and Dedicated offerings with predictable behavior (KV cache mapping, quantized variants, and tracing compatibility).

High-level ask: start a technical integration track to certify MapleBridge SDKs against Redwood's runtime variants and produce a lightweight compatibility matrix + mutual action plan (MAP). Goals:
- Confirm tracing hook semantics and span propagation across Redwood routing/fallbacks
- Validate prompt-tooling structured outputs (function-calling / tool manifests) end-to-end
- Quantization/runtime caveats for edge deployments (private/on-prem)
- Deliverables: compatibility matrix, a small POC (LangChain + Redwood hosted), and an SOW for joint co-marketing once certified

I've attached a one-pager 'integration-outline.pdf' that shows the scope.

Would you be available for a 45-60 minute engineering deep-dive next week? Our engineers can demo the tracing shim and a small workload reproducer.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Head of Partnerships | MapleBridge
https://maplebridge.ai

Attachment: integration-outline.pdf (pdf, 230KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@maplebridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MapleBridge + Redwood: runtime curation & SDK integration

Daniel — thanks for reaching out and for the outline. This is squarely the kind of ISV integration we want to standardize. Happy to run a technical track.

Suggested agenda for the deep-dive (45 min):
1) Quick intros + current customer signals (5 min)
2) MapleBridge SDK architecture & tracing shim demo (10 min)
3) Redwood runtime compatibility points (auth, KV cache, quantization, sequence-length behavior) (15 min)
4) POC acceptance criteria and MAP / SOW next steps (10 min)

Can you share a short compatibility matrix in advance (SDK versions supported, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter entry points, required env vars, and if you rely on gRPC vs HTTP for tracing export)? That will help us scope which runtime variants to test (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Proposed times (PST): Mon 10/13 10:30am, Tue 10/14 2:00pm, Wed 10/15 9:00am. What works for your eng lead?

Looping in Marissa (partnerships/partner-engineering) and Kim (runtime product) — Marissa/Kim, please flag any pre-reqs from the Redwood side (NDA, network allowlist, test account creation). Jonas, could you capture perf targets we should try to meet for the POC (p95 token latency, tokens/sec baseline)?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of ISV Alliances | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@maplebridge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: MapleBridge Partnerships <partnerships@maplebridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MapleBridge + Redwood: runtime curation & SDK integration

Vanessa — great, thanks. Tue 10/14 2:00pm PST works for our eng lead (Aisha Patel, cc'd on our side in calendar invite). Per your request, attaching an initial compatibility file 'compatibility-matrix.csv' and a draft SOW (v0.1). Quick notes pulled from the matrix:
- LangChain adapters: supported for versions 0.0.186 -> 0.0.202 (we vendor a shim under maplebridge/langchain-adapter). Adapter relies on HTTP-based span export compatible with OpenTelemetry collector endpoints (we can switch to gRPC if you prefer).
- LlamaIndex: adapters for LlamaIndex v0.8+ with a JSON manifest for structured index serialization (we include tools to export store snapshots).
- Tracing: we emit semantic span attributes: 'maple.step', 'maple.tool', and propagate 'traceparent' header. For runtimes that rewrite headers (proxies / API gateways), we provide a fallback token-based correlation header.
- Function calling: we follow the 'tool manifest' pattern with explicit schema in the payload; we've validated function-calling round trips against two generic hosts.

Network / security caveats:
- For Private deployments: MapleBridge's agent needs an outbound allowlist to our collector endpoint or you can provide a private collector endpoint.
- For Dedicated: our POC needs a test model endpoint and a token with dev-level scopes.

Attachments included: compatibility-matrix.csv, SOW_Redwood_MapleBridge_v0.1.pdf.

We'll also attach a small reproducer repo link in the calendar invite so the engs can run end-to-end in under 20 minutes.

Looking forward to the sync.

Thanks,
Daniel

Attachment: compatibility-matrix.csv (csv, 12KB)
Attachment: SOW_Redwood_MapleBridge_v0.1.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Marissa/Kim — can you review the attached MAPlebridge_Mutual_Action_Plan.docx and confirm owners? Jonas — please add perf targets for the POC (p95 token latency target and throughput baseline) and drop a short checklist in the Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ISV-43.
